l0.shape: Two separate systems that share only a JSON format: a Claude Code skill (instructions + two Python scripts) and a static viewer on GitHub Pages.
l0.summary: Strata maps a repository's architecture at five zoom levels, from a one-line overview (L0) to symbol-level deep dives (L4). The skill tells Claude Code to build a free AST graph with graphify, roll it up with arch_digest.py, check every boundary claim against the code, and write a strata/1 JSON. strata_pack.py validates that JSON (including the confidence score), saves it, writes an optional Markdown report and prints a link. The link carries the whole map in the URL fragment, so no server ever sees it. The viewer is plain JavaScript that draws the map by hand-drawn style with dagre and rough.js.

deep_dives.title: Share links with no server
deep_dives.markdown:
## Encoding
`strata_pack.py` dumps the JSON compactly, compresses it with **raw deflate** (`zlib.compressobj(9, DEFLATED, -15)`) and encodes it as unpadded **base64url** (`strata_pack.py:302-306`). The link is `<viewer>#d=<data>` (`:307`).

## Why the fragment
Browsers do not send the part after `#` to the server, so GitHub Pages never receives the map. The viewer decodes it with the browser's `DecompressionStream('deflate-raw')` (`docs/app.js:61`).

## Limits
| Limit | Where |
|---|---|
| Links over 60,000 chars are not printed; drop the file instead | `strata_pack.py:34`, `:313` |
| The report embeds the link only when it is under 2,000 chars | `strata_pack.py:311` |

## Other sources
`?map=` accepts only `[a-z0-9-]` names from `examples/` (`docs/app.js:99`). `?src=` accepts https or same-origin URLs only, and fetches with no credentials and no referrer (`docs/app.js:101-103`).

deep_dives.title: Rendering untrusted maps
deep_dives.markdown: A map can come from anyone, so the viewer treats it as hostile. | Control | Where | |---|---| | CSP: scripts only from self and jsDelivr; no inline script; `object-src 'none'`; `base-uri 'none'` | `docs/index.html:8` | | Pinned library versions with SRI hashes | `docs/index.html:118-121` | | Text goes in through `textContent` via `el()` | `docs/app.js:22` | | Raw HTML in Markdown is escaped before parsing | `docs/app.js:19` | | Parsed Markdown is sanitised; `style`, `form`, `input` and style attributes removed | `docs/app.js:323` | | JSON shape is checked before drawing | `docs/app.js:67` | The escape step matters: without it, raw `` would reach DOMPurify's parser, and only the CSP would stop it.

deep_dives.title: The confidence check
deep_dives.markdown:
The rubric is in `SKILL.md`. `check_confidence()` (`strata_pack.py:51`) enforces the parts a script can see.

**Errors (pack fails):** no score, score not an integer 0–100, label not matching the band (High 80–100, Med 50–79, Low 0–49), or no basis.

**Warnings:** the share of links and flow steps with no evidence or with `inferred: true` is over 20% while the score is High, or over 50% while it is Med (`strata_pack.py:76-82`).

The check cannot tell whether the evidence lines are correct; that still depends on the verification step.
